aspects.says: A GenericPackager reads each field's number, length and encoding class from an XML definition, so a message format can change without Java code.
aspects.reason: it needs a packager definition file, and a graded run has none; the exercise uses a packager built in code instead

aspects.says: jPOS components such as channels, packagers and fields can be created from their class names.
aspects.reason: the page itself calls it incidental to message handling, and the ISOFactory class it shows is not in jPOS 2.1.7

aspects.says: Messages of one kind are built from a named template that fixes the MTI and the constant fields, so each new message only adds what varies per transaction.
A packager turns a message into the bytes that go on the wire and back, and unpacking what it packed gives the same fields again.
